rationale: Start with a broad gradient at an intermediate temperature to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds and reveal the retention range and critical separations. The remaining high-organic hold allows strongly retained compounds time to elute.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin can be retained. Keep the starting composition and temperature fixed to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Use an intermediate gradient duration to recover separation in the crowded middle group while keeping the last peak much earlier than in injection 1. This tests the tradeoff between resolution recovery and the time penalty.

Increase temperature by 5 °C to test whether selectivity improves for the remaining critical pair while maintaining the short analysis time. Only a modest resolution gain is needed to reach full resolution without a time penalty.

Test a 5 °C decrease from the best method because warming sharply worsened the critical separation. This will establish whether cooling resolves that pair without creating another limiting pair or exceeding the penalty-free time window.

Use a shallower gradient at the best temperature to improve the critical middle-group separation, while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the longer retention time. This targets full resolution with the last peak still near the penalty-free time window.

Raise the starting organic fraction one grid step to bring the last peak below 10 minutes and eliminate the remaining time penalty. The slightly shallower gradient may preserve the critical-pair resolution, while the early peaks currently have ample separation.

Test a shallower gradient to increase the critical-pair resolution margin, offsetting the expected retention increase with a higher starting organic fraction. The aim is to retain the maximum CRF while improving separation robustness.

Preserve injection 7’s starting composition, gradient slope, and temperature while lowering the final organic fraction. Since all peaks previously eluted before this gradient would end, this method should retain CRF 1.000 with a less organic-rich final hold.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope relative to injection 8 to improve its marginal critical-pair resolution. The last peak is expected to remain near but below 10 minutes, potentially retaining CRF 1.000 with a larger separation margin.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a faster, high-temperature alternative for a potentially shorter method with full resolution. Moving well beyond the near-coelution at 45 °C may separate the critical compounds after an elution-order reversal, though other pairs must be checked.

Back off from 60 °C to relieve the newly limiting coelution, and use a longer gradient to increase separation. This tests an alternative selectivity region that may deliver full resolution with a last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Test a slightly steeper gradient at 55 °C, where the critical compounds appear to have reversed elution order relative to 40 °C. This may improve their separation while shortening the analysis, although the other middle-group separations must also remain above 1.5.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the faster maximum-score method can be shortened further. The critical separations have little margin, so this run will check whether the accompanying change in gradient slope preserves full resolution.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope to recover the separation lost in injection 14 while retaining its higher starting organic fraction. This targets a balance between the two critical pairs with a last-peak time still close to the faster maximum-score method.

Lower the final organic fraction one more step to improve the limiting separation beyond 1.5. The other critical pair changed little in the previous step, so this may restore CRF 1.000 with a larger resolution margin than injection 13.

Combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to seek larger margins for both critical separations at 55 °C. This tests another route to retaining CRF 1.000 while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Lengthen injection 17’s gradient to improve its limiting separation while preserving the favorable margin of the other critical pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, offering a chance to recover CRF 1.000 with improved separation margins.

Make the gradient slightly shallower to increase the limiting resolution in injection 18 and better balance its two critical pairs. The projected last-peak time remains below 10 minutes, so this may retain CRF 1.000 with a larger minimum-resolution margin.

Use a gradient slope between those of injections 18 and 19 to balance their two critical separations. This should keep the last peak below 10 minutes while potentially increasing the minimum resolution slightly and retaining CRF 1.000.

Test whether a shallower gradient resolves the middle-group coelution seen in the fast 60 °C run while preserving that temperature’s favorable separation elsewhere. This may provide larger resolution margins at CRF 1.000, provided the last peak remains below 10 minutes.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 16 to strengthen its weaker middle-group separation while retaining the higher-organic final hold. This should keep the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes and may preserve the maximum CRF with useful resolution margins.

Use a gradient slope between injections 15 and 16 to balance the two critical separations while shortening retention relative to injection 16. This targets another maximum-CRF method with the last peak around 7.8 minutes.

Use a gradient slope close to injection 20’s balanced optimum, but reach a lower final organic fraction sooner. All peaks are expected to elute before the gradient ends, potentially preserving CRF 1.000 and a minimum resolution near 1.7.

Test a gradient slope between injections 19 and 20, where both critical separations should retain comfortable margins above 1.5. This final method is expected to preserve the maximum CRF of 1.000 with the last peak below 10 minutes.
